Basavaraja, J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

For the death of one Abdulrahaman Tambadi in the road traffic accident on 17th June, 2019, the petitioners, who are wife, unmarried daughter and the minor son of the deceased, filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 before the Tribunal.

The Tribunal allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.18,21,200/-
NC: 2023:KHC-D:10650-DB with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
2. Being aggrieved by the quantum, so also, as to liability of the compensation the appellant-NWKRTC has preferred the present appeal.

The Divisional Controller vs Smt. Naseem W/O Abdulrahaman Tambadi on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105023435/
2 3.
We have heard the learned counsel for the parties.

Sri I.C. Patil, learned counsel appearing for the appellant- NWKRTC submits that the Tribunal ought to have dismissed the claim petition for non-joinder of necessary parties, i.e. owner and insured of vehicle baring motorcycle No.KA-22/ES-5729.

He further submits that as the bus is a non-stop bus and there is no Conductor in the bus, the driver of the bus,following traffic rules and regulations, has stopped the bus on the extreme left side of the road for issuance of tickets, but the rider of the motorcycle came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the hindside of the bus which resulted in the accident.
But the Tribunal as erroneously come to the conclusion that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus.

The evidence on record like Exhibit P3-Panchanama, Exhibit P6-IMV Report, Exhibit P7- NC:
2023:KHC-D:10650-DB Charge sheet and Exhibit P1-charge sheet filed against the deceased motorcyclist; Exhibit R2-hand sketch and Exhibit P4- photo disclose that the rider of motorcycle himself was rash and negligent in riding who caused the accident.
The Tribunal has not properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts.

Further, the Tribunal has grossly erred in awarding the compensation of Rs.18,21,200/-
in the absence of any in the absence of any occupation and on all these grounds sought to allow the appeal.

4. As against this, the learned counsel appearing for the claimants submits that the Tribunal considering the oral and documentary evidence has awarded just and reasonable compensation and there is no ground for interference and hence sought for dismissal of appeal.

5. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, the following points would arise for our consideration in this appeal:
1.
Whether the appellant has made out a ground for interference with the impugned judgment NC: 2023:KHC-D:10650-DB and award as to quantum of compensation and liability?
2. What order or award?

6. Our answer for the above points are as under:
Point No.1: in the negative;
Point No.2: as per final order Regarding Point No.1:
7. Having given our anxious consideration go the arguments advanced by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, we have perused the impugned judgment and award.
The Divisional Controller vs Smt. Naseem W/O Abdulrahaman Tambadi on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105023435/
3

The Tribunal, at paragraphs 11 to 15, has observed as under:
"11. Eyewitness to the accident by name Jayanulla S/o Yusuf Shahabajkhan is examined on behalf of the petitioners.
He is also cited as CW -6 in Ex-D1 Charge sheet.
Pw-2 Jayanulla has deposed reason for accident is parking KSRTC bus.
I have perused the documentary evidence in detail.
It is clear from Ex.P1/FIR that, the case is filed against both drivers i.e., deceased Abdulrahaman Imamsab Tambadi and RW1/Basavaraj Adappa Haleuppar.
One Saleem Abdulajeej Inamdar has given first information to the Belagavi Traffic police North and accordingly, Crime No.79/2019 has been registered.
The investigation officer has invested the matter, and he has filed charge sheet against both deceased NC: 2023:KHC-D:10650-DB Abdulrahaman Imamsab Tambadi and RW1/Basavaraj Adappa Haleuppar.
Ex.P7 is the copy of the charge sheet filed against the driver of KSRTC Bus.
Ex.P7 shows that RW1- Basavaraj is guilty of offence punishable U/Sec.283,336, 304(A).
Further respondent of 2019 has produced the copy of the charge sheet filed against the deceased at Ex.R1.
Ex.R1 shows that abated charge sheet is filed against the deceased for the offences punishable U/Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC.
The charge sheet is against both deceased Abdulrahaman Imamsab Tambadi and RW1/Basavaraj Adappa Haleuppar.
It is well settled principles of law that Tribunal has to assess the evidence independently and give finding who is negligent.
Ex.R2 is the sketch of place of accident.
It is clear from the Ex.R2 that KSRTC Bus was parked by leaving 4 feet from the edge of the national highway.
It can be taken note of that, Bus will be almost 8 to 10 feet in width.

The I.O.
has shown width of National Highway as 42 feet.
Width of road between spot of accident and divider is 34 feet.
So, it is clear that Bus was parked from 4 feet to 12 feet on the NH-4 which is 42 feet in width.
It is argued on behalf of the respondent that there was sufficient space available to the deceased Abdulrahaman Imamsab Tambadi to pass the Bus i.e., almost 34 feet.
Hence, deceased was negligent.
I am unable to accept the arguments of the counsel for respondent for the simple reason that in national highway vehicles will be passing with great speed.
One cannot take immediate right turn during the traffic hours to pass the vehicle which is parked on the national highway.
Just because, sufficient space of 2019 was available to pass, this tribunal cannot NC: 2023:KHC-D:10650-DB hold deceased is negligent.
It must be considered that at the time of accident whether national highway was free of traffic or not.
If there are traffic in the national highway then it may not be possible for one to take right turn immediately by noticing the parked vehicle.
So, this tribunal cannot come to conclusion that deceased Abdul, could have avoided the accident by taking right turn to pass the parked Bus.
12. Rule 15 of Rules of the Road Regulations, 1989 deals with parking of vehicle.

sentences.text: So it is clear from Rule 15(2)(iv) & (x) of Road Regulations, 1989 that driver of a motor vehicle shall not park his vehicle in a main road or one carrying fast traffic or where parking in prohibited.
National high-way is meant for speed driving and one cannot park vehicle in the national highway except in the places meant for parking vehicle called parking zones.
The parking of the vehicle in national highway by itself amounts to negligent act.
RW1 has admitted in the examination that there are parking zones between Belagavi and Hubli in the national highway.
If RW1 was driver cum conductor, then he would have parked the vehicle in some of these parking zones and would have given ticket.
But, he has not done so.
Apart this as per Ex-R 2 Hand sketch there is service road.
If issuance of ticket is necessary, then driver would have parked the vehicle in service road.

Counsel for Respondent has argued that if vehicle had parked in service road, then traffic would have The Divisional Controller vs Smt. Naseem W/O Abdulrahaman Tambadi on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105023435/
5 effected.

sentences.text:
I am unable to accept this argument since parking of vehicle is governed NC:
2023:KHC-D:10650-DB under Motor Vehicle Act, Rule and Road Regulations.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Act, Rule and Road Regulations
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: No one can park vehicle in any place of his own wish & choice.
It has to be in accordance with the rules.

When driver of KSRTC Bus had parked the vehicle in no parking zone, deceased who is coming on national highway which is meant for speed driving, could have though that such a vehicle will be parked on the national highway.
Apart from this petitioners have examined PW2 who is eyewitness to the accident, and he has deposed that Bus was parked in negligent manner.
So, considering this aspect, I am of the opinion that one cannot hold that deceased was negligent in driving the vehicle though charge sheet is filed against him.

14. Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in decision reported in 2019(2) T.A.C.282 (Kar) Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance company limited vs Savita & others has dealt with similar kind of case wherein abated charge sheet was filed against the deceased who has dashed to parked truck & held as under :-
" 10.

entities.text: 2019(2) T.A.C.282 (Kar) Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance company limited vs Savita & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The accident is not in dispute.

The only question which is raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that abated charge sheet has been filed against the deceased and the deceased has also contributed to the alleged accident.

He would further contend that the lorry was parked on its right side by following the traffic rules as - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10650-DB such, liability ought not to have been fixed on the appellantinsurance company.

As could be seen from the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and the documents, the Tribunal after considering all the facts and circumstances has come to the conclusion that the driver of the lorry was negligent and as such, liability has been fixed on him.

On perusal of Exs.P12 and P14 it would indicate that charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the lorry and the driver of the lorry had pleaded guilty and he was convicted for the offence for having parked the lorry in the middle of the road and for causing obstruction for free movement of the vehicle which is supported by the evidence of PWs.3 and 4.

Even Ex.P3- spot panchanama discloses that the driver has parked the lorry two feet away from the mid line and it also indicates that the driver of the lorry has parked the said lorry without any parking lights and domestic lights or any other indication for having parked the said lorry in the said place.
Admittedly, the said accident has taken place on the said road during night hours.

The driver of the lorry has parked the lorry without any just cause and without putting parking lights or domestic lights or any indication, all these facts indicate the negligence on the part of the driver of - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10650-DB lorry and there is no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.

The Divisional Controller vs Smt. Naseem W/O Abdulrahaman Tambadi on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105023435/
6
Though the abated charge sheet is said to have been filed against the deceased, the records clearly indicates that the driver of the lorry has pleaded guilty and has not contested the case.
Under the circumstances, fixing of entire liability on the appellant-insurance company appears to be justifiable.

15. In another Judgment in between Renuka W/o Shekarappa Kathariki & others Vs The Commandant, India Reserve Battalion Munirabad & others (MFA 102501/2015) Hon'ble High Court has considered similar situation and held as under :-
18.

entities.text: Renuka W/o Shekarappa Kathariki & others Vs The Commandant, India Reserve Battalion Munirabad & others (MFA 102501/2015)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, the Tribunal could not have denied the compensation.
Because involving of two vehicles composite negligence should have been examined by the Tribunal.
Therefore, the Government Insurance Department as well as insurance company of the lorry would be liable to pay the compensation amount.
It is only in case of the jeep driver this contingency would arise.

In this regard, the judgment of this Court dated 28.03.2019 in M.F.A.No. 24179/2012 and connected matters can be referred. At paragraph 94 of the judgment reads as under:
"94. Section 122 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 deals with leaving vehicles in dangerous position.

It - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10650-DB states that no person in charge of a motor vehicle shall cause or allow the vehicle or any trailer to be abandoned or to remain at rest on any public place in such a position or in such a condition or in such circumstances as to cause or likely to cause danger, obstruction or undue inconvenience to other users of the public place or to the passengers.

The owner of the vehicle has the right to driver the vehicle on the road and also the right to part the vehicle, but the parking of the vehicle cannot cause any danger or obstruction to other passersby or passengers.
This is a restriction on the road to park the vehicle.
The aforesaid restriction on the road to part a vehicle is reasonable restriction and emanates from duty to take care."
19. Therefore, a strict liability is cast on the person who parks his vehicle on the Highway.
It cannot be argued that since the accident had occurred during day time, vehicle was visible and hence negligence could not be cast on the truck driver .
It is important to note that if the truck had not parked at that place, probably the fatal injuries would not have been caused to the inmates of the jeep.
It is in that context, we hold 100% negligence on the truck driver only.

On re-appreciation, re-examination and re- The Divisional Controller vs Smt. Naseem W/O Abdulrahaman Tambadi on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105023435/
7 consideration of the evidence on record, we do not find any illegalities/legal infirmities in the finding given by the Tribunal as to rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of NWKRTC bus.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts.

Further, with regard to quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal, relying on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. NANU RAM AND OTHERS reported in (2018)18 SCC 130, has awarded just compensation.

entities.text: MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. NANU RAM AND OTHERS reported in (2018)18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, we do not find any material to interfere with the impugned judgment and award on that point also.
Hence, we answer point No.1 in the negative.

Regarding Point No.2:
9.

For the aforesaid reasons and discussions, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER 1. Appeal is dismissed.
Amount in deposit if any, is directed to be transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.
